headline: Traffic relief: Congestion charging zone launched to limit private cars
summary: A new system is being introduced to reduce traffic jams by charging private vehicles entering specific high-traffic areas.
details: A congestion charging zone has been introduced to manage the pressure of private cars and reduce traffic congestion in the city.
The initiative aims to discourage the use of private vehicles in heavily congested areas, encouraging more people to shift to public transport.
Under this system, private cars entering designated zones will be required to pay a fee, acting as a deterrent to unnecessary trips.
Officials believe this measure will help streamline traffic flow and reduce thet travel time for commuters across the city.
caption:
Tired of endless traffic jams? A new congestion charging zone is here to limit private cars.

A congestion charging zone has been introduced to manage the pressure of private cars and reduce traffic congestion in the city.

The initiative aims to discourage the use of private vehicles in heavily congested areas, encouraging more people to shift to public transport.

Under this system, private cars entering designated zones will be required to pay a fee, acting as a deterrent to unnecessary trips.

Officials believe this measure will help streamline traffic flow and reduce thet travel time for commuters across the city.

headline_marked: Two Bangladeshis [[tricked into joining Russian army]] now in Ukraine jail
headline: Two Bangladeshis tricked into joining Russian army now in Ukraine jail
summary: The men claim a broker promised them passage to Italy for Tk 10 lakh, but instead forced them into military contracts and sent them to the frontlines.
details: Kamrul Hasan and Suman Shahriar, two Bangladeshi nationals, are currently held in a Ukrainian prisoner-of-war jail after being allegedly deceived by a broker.
The men claim a broker named 'Udbegh Gamer' promised to take them from Russia to Italy for Tk 10 lakh each, taking an initial payment of Tk 5 lakh from both.
Instead of travel documents, they allege they were forced to sign Russian military contracts written in a language they did not understand and were taken to a camp in Tula.
After 35 days of military training, they were sent toward Ukraine. They claim they fled their mission on March 12 after facing severe food and water shortages.
After walking approximately 100 kilometers toward the Ukrainian side, they were detained by Ukrainian soldiers and taken to a detention facility.
The Bangladesh embassy in Poland, which manages Ukraine affairs, stated they are aware of the situation and are in communication with the victims' families to facilitate their rescue.
caption:
Promised a path to Italy for Tk 10 lakh, two Bangladeshis ended up in a Ukrainian POW jail after being tricked into joining the Russian army.

Kamrul Hasan and Suman Shahriar, two Bangladeshi nationals, are currently held in a Ukrainian prisoner-of-war jail after being allegedly deceived by a broker.

The men claim a broker named 'Udbegh Gamer' promised to take them from Russia to Italy for Tk 10 lakh each, taking an initial payment of Tk 5 lakh from both.

Instead of travel documents, they allege they were forced to sign Russian military contracts written in a language they did not understand and were taken to a camp in Tula.

After 35 days of military training, they were sent toward Ukraine. They claim they fled their mission on March 12 after facing severe food and water shortages.

After walking approximately 100 kilometers toward the Ukrainian side, they were detained by Ukrainian soldiers and taken to a detention facility.

The Bangladesh embassy in Poland, which manages Ukraine affairs, stated they are aware of the situation and are in communication with the victims' families to facilitate their rescue.
